key_claims: Gorbachev told Karmal in March 1985 that Soviet troops could not remain in Afghanistan forever.
Moscow conditioned withdrawal on a political settlement with guarantees against outside interference, blaming Pakistan and the US for obstruction.
Seven regiments were announced for withdrawal at Vladivostok in July 1986; six regiments' withdrawal was announced complete in November 1986.
On 2 Feb 1988 the USSR and Afghanistan set 15 May 1988 as start of a ten-month withdrawal.
The Geneva Accords were signed 14 April 1988 and entered into force 15 May 1988, after which Moscow accused Pakistan of violations.
The Soviet government repeatedly accused Pakistan and the US of violating the April 1988 Geneva agreements by backing the Afghan opposition.
The USSR completed troop withdrawal on 15 February 1989 and urged an inter-Afghan settlement and coalition government.
Moscow treated the Kabul government of Najibullah as the only legal government and rejected the opposition's transitional government in March 1989.
Soviet diplomat Vorontsov met the seven-party opposition in Saudi Arabia in Dec 1988 about Soviet prisoners and settlement.
Gorbachev admitted the decision to send troops to Afghanistan was made in secret without leadership discussion, and the Congress of People's Deputies condemned it in Dec 1989.
